q.t: A fractal is a shape that:
o: Contains smaller copies of itself again and again
q.e: Self-similarity at smaller and smaller scales: ferns, trees, coastlines.

q.t: In the Sierpinski Carpet, a square is cut into how many equal squares at each step?
q.e: A 3 × 3 grid; the middle one is removed, leaving 8.

q.t: How many squares remain at step 1 of the Sierpinski Carpet?
q.e: 9 minus the removed middle square.

q.t: In the Sierpinski Gasket, joining the midpoints of a triangle makes how many small triangles?
q.e: Three corner triangles and one middle triangle, all equilateral and identical.

q.t: How many faces does a cube have?
q.e: Top, bottom, front, back, left, right.

q.t: How many edges does a cube have?
q.e: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, 4 upright.

q.t: How many different nets does a cube have?
q.e: Counting rotations and flips as the same net.

q.t: Which solid has NO net?
q.e: A curved ball can't be flattened without gaps or overlaps.

q.t: The net of a cylinder is two circles and a:
q.e: The curved side unrolls into a rectangle whose width is the circumference 2πr.

q.t: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple shows fractal-like design. Where is it?
q.e: Completed around 1025 CE in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh.

q.t: How many squares remain at step 2 of the Sierpinski Carpet?
q.e: Each of the 8 squares becomes 8: Rₙ = 8ⁿ.

q.t: How many holes are there at step 2 of the Sierpinski Carpet?
q.e: The 1 old hole stays and each of the 8 squares adds a new one.

q.t: How many triangles remain at step 3 of the Sierpinski Gasket?
q.e: Each step triples the triangles: 3ⁿ.

q.t: A Koch snowflake starts as a triangle (3 sides). How many sides at step 1?
q.e: Each side becomes 4 shorter sides.

q.t: How many edges does a pentagonal prism have?
q.e: 5 on top, 5 on the bottom, 5 joining them: 3n.

q.t: How many vertices does a hexagonal pyramid have?
q.e: 6 base corners plus the apex.

q.t: For a prism, pyramid or cube, F + V − E equals:
q.e: Euler's rule, e.g. cube 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.

q.t: How many nets does a regular tetrahedron have?
q.e: A big triangle split into 4, or a strip of 4 triangles.

q.t: The shortest path between two points on a box's surface is found by:
o: Unfolding it into a net and joining them with a straight line
Measuring the diagonal of the box
q.e: Unfolding keeps lengths, so the shortest surface path becomes a straight segment on some net.

q.t: The projection of a segment onto a plane is:
q.e: The segment is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose leg is the projection.

q.t: Area remaining in the Sierpinski Carpet at step n (start 1):
q.e: Each step keeps 8 of the 9 equal parts of every square.

q.t: Area remaining in the Sierpinski Gasket at step 2 (start 1):
q.e: Each step keeps 3 of 4 parts: (3/4)².

q.t: Perimeter of the Koch snowflake at step 1 (starting side 1):
q.e: 12 sides of length 1/3.

q.t: As the step number grows, the Koch snowflake's perimeter:
q.e: It is multiplied by 4/3 at every step.

q.t: How many holes at step 3 of the Sierpinski Gasket?
A segment's projection has the same length as the segment exactly when it is:
q.e: Then the right triangle is flat — the projection IS the segment.

q.t: A parallelogram's shadow in sunlight (on a plane perpendicular to the rays) is always a:
q.e: Parallel lines project to parallel lines.

q.t: In an isometric drawing of a cube, its edges are drawn:
q.e: 'Isometric' means equal measure.

q.t: Which can NOT be a cube net?
o: Five squares in a row with one square attached
A cross shape (row of 4 with one above and one below)
Two rows of 3, shifted by one
q.e: Five in a row would wrap round and overlap.

q.t: A cone's net is a circle and a:
q.e: Every point on the base rim is the same slant distance from the apex, so the side unrolls onto a circle around the apex.

q.t: An ant's route unfolds into a right triangle with legs 24 cm and 32 cm. How long is it (in cm)?
How many sides does the Koch snowflake have at step 3?
How many squares remain at step 3 of the Sierpinski Carpet?
How many edges does a 10-sided prism have?
How many faces does a 10-sided pyramid have?
q.e: 10 triangular faces plus the base.

q.t: Besides the 5 flat shapes, how many more ways are there to glue 4 cubes face to face?
q.e: The 3D 'tripod' and two twisted shapes that are mirror images.

q.t: Why can the 'impossible triangle' be drawn but not built?
o: The isometric drawing hides depth, so far-apart edges appear joined
q.e: Every corner is buildable; only the whole loop contradicts itself.

q.t: A torch close to an object makes a shadow bigger than the projection. As the torch moves very far away, the shadow:
q.e: Far-away light rays are nearly parallel — like sunlight.

q.t: The top view of a cone standing on its base is:
o: A circle (with the apex at its centre)
q.e: Looking down you see the round base and the apex over its centre.

q.t: The Sierpinski Carpet's area at step n is (8/9)ⁿ. As n grows very large, the area:
q.e: Multiplying by 8/9 again and again shrinks it towards 0.
